title: RiskEvaluationResult
description: Normative shape of a Tier 2 verdict, for approval/contracts/risk-judge@0.1.0. Every path out of the evaluation produces one of these documents, including every failure: a timeout, an unreachable provider, a refused connection and an unparseable response all yield a result with decision ESCALATE_USER and isFallback true, never an absence and never an approval (INV-AP-12). The decision vocabulary is closed at three values, and no value in it means allow-an-operation-Tier-1-refused - the judge can hold or narrow what Tier 1 permitted and can never widen it (INV-AP-11).

decision.description: The verdict. Closed at three values: adding a fourth is a MAJOR bump, because a verdict the calling wrapper does not recognise is one it would have to interpret, and the only safe interpretation of an unknown verdict is to stop.

riskLevel.description: How the judge categorised the operation. Explanatory rather than operative: what happens to the call is decided by `decision` alone, so a mismatch between level and decision is a reporting fault and never a licence to act. The measured spike exercised LOW, HIGH and UNCERTAIN (spikes/SP-10-risk-judge/src/types.ts); SAFE and MEDIUM are specified here and are so far unexercised.

reasoning.description: One line recorded with the ledger record for this call, and shown to the user when the call is escalated. It explains a verdict already reached; nothing here is read back as input to any later decision.

isFallback.description: True when this result came from the fail-closed path rather than from model inference. It is required rather than optional so that a verdict can never be read as considered when it was in fact a failure: an audit that cannot tell the two apart cannot tell a working judge from an unreachable one.

latencyMs.description: How long the evaluation took, including a fail-closed path that ended early. Recorded so that the latency thresholds in verification.md are measured from what the product observed rather than from what a provider reported.
